timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So Azure Policy just... blocks bad stuff?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Depends on the effect. Pick wrong and you block everything or enforce nothing.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Deny stops creation or updates that violate policy. DenyAction stops lifecycle actions like deletion.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What if I only want to know, not block?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Audit writes a warning. AuditIfNotExists flags missing things like diagnostic settings.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Modify changes properties. DeployIfNotExists deploys what's missing. Append adds properties.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Disabled pauses evaluation. Manual needs attestation for procedural controls.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Do effects run in some order?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Fixed order: disabled, append/modify, deny, audit, manual, auditIfNotExists, denyAction.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Audit first, measure impact, remediate, then flip to Deny.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So compliance is a journey, not a switch.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. And evaluation never sleeps — it runs every 24 hours.
